items.title: Wings of Change 10 Years of Redefining Regional Air Connectivity through UDAN
items.summary: 20 OCT 2026 10:17AM by PIB Delhi UDAN completes ten years in 2026. Over the past decade, it has expanded India’s regional aviation network, connecting unserved & underserved regions and improving access to air travel. Regional connectivity has supported tourism, medical access, agricultural trade and local employment, with airports such as Tezu, Deoghar and Kishangarh illustrating its impact.

facts.text: In line with this objective, the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS), also known as UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik), was launched on 21 October 2016.
India is now the world’s third-largest domestic aviation market , with operational airports increasing from 74 in 2014 to 166 till date .
UDAN entered its operational stage with the inauguration of the first RCS-UDAN flight from Shimla to Delhi in April 2017 .
Flights Operated: More than 3.68 lakh flights have been operated under the scheme.

items.title: PM Modi-led Govt is striving to make India a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge and strength with a commitment to global peace & well-being of humanity: Raksha Mantri
items.summary: 20 OCT 2026 8:53PM by PIB Delhi “Guided by the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam , India aspires to become a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge & strength with a commitment to global peace and the well-being of humanity,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing the Indian diaspora in Dushanbe, Tajikistan on October 20, 2026.

facts.text: Highlighting India’s growth trajectory, Raksha Mantri stated that the country contributes more than 16 per cent to global economic growth and is growing at approximately 7.8 per cent, even as several major economies face a slowdown.

Referring to the changing global trade landscape, the Raksha Mantri said that India has entered into Free Trade Agreements with 38 countries, opening new markets for Indian manufacturers and producers.

He stated that the India-UK and India-EU trade agreements, which are expected to eliminate tariffs on 99 per cent of Indian exports to these markets, would strengthen the country’s trade prospects and global economic partnerships.
Raksha Mantri noted that the current account deficit, which exceeded four per cent of GDP 12-13 years ago, declined to 0.61 per cent in the previous financial year.
